short: The formal surrender of the Swedish dominions of Estonia and Livonia to the Russian Empire.
full:
During 1710, following the capture of Riga and Reval (Tallinn), the local Baltic German nobility and the cities of Estonia and Livonia formally capitulated to Russian forces. This marked the end of Swedish administration in the provinces, which had been among the most economically valuable parts of the Swedish Empire.

In exchange for their surrender, Peter the Great guaranteed the Baltic German elite their traditional privileges, local autonomy, and the preservation of the Lutheran faith. This pragmatic settlement secured the loyalty of the Baltic nobility to the Russian Tsar, providing Russia with capable administrators and military officers for generations to come.
